# FDG9008

> DO provide properties with getters and setters corresponding to all parameters of aggregate component constructors.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.1.3 Aggregate Component Guidelines.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Not an analyzer candidate: only aggregate components need a settable property for each constructor parameter, while factored types should have get-only properties for settings that cannot change (section 9.1.1), and whether a type is an aggregate component is a design judgment. FDG5046 checks that a constructor parameter that sets a property has its name.

## From the book

It should always be possible to use the default constructor and then set some properties instead of calling a parameterized constructor.

```csharp
public class MessageQueue {
   public MessageQueue() { ... }
   public MessageQueue(string path) { ... }

   public string Path { get { ... } set { ... } }
}
```
